neighbours.label: the noun or phrase end that closes a time-span or periodical reference ('for three weeks', '12 months', 'the August issue')
fire: The volunteers took the supplement daily for six weeks before testing.
Mice were kept in the cold room for two days and then examined.
The results were published in the March issue of the journal.
Participants were tracked for five years after the first visit.
The bridge will be closed for three months while workers repair it.
The interview appears in this week's issue of the magazine.
Seeds were soaked in water for 48 hours before planting.
Her contract was extended by another two years last spring.
quiet: The volunteers took six tablets of the supplement before testing.
Mice were kept in two cages in the cold room and then examined.
The results were published on page twelve of the journal.
Participants were tracked with five sensors after the first visit.
The bridge will be closed to trucks while workers repair it.
The interview appears in the culture section of the magazine.
Seeds were soaked in two litres of water before planting.
Her contract was extended to cover another two shops last spring.

notes: Card peaks: ' months', ' weeks', ' year', ' issue' (journal issue) and punctuation after a duration. Probe: 'followed for 12 months.' 0.31 vs '12 tablets' 0.02; 'current issue' 0.73. Near misses keep a number + noun but not a time span.
